what: Pane median / that same car's own paint median, in LINEAR light, inside one image. The first photographic anchor this project has for CAR GLASS; every previous car anchor was for wheels.
why: Ten rounds of car work argued about whether the glazing was too dark with no reference. Found by a blind reviewer in the closing round, in reprojected Mapillary spheres of real Sarasota streets that were already in the repo.
method: A ratio inside one image, so the unknown camera response cancels to first order. Files are gnomonic resamples of JPEGs and the response is assumed sRGB; the views are 4-channel where the render captures are 3-channel, so any probe must read png.channels.

verdict: Before this round the windscreen sat at the level of heavily privacy-tinted SUV glass, and windscreens are never privacy-tinted - darker relative to its own paint than any clear glazing measurable in the reference. Shipped, it sits between clear side glass (0.030) and a clear rear screen with a lit cabin (0.11-0.13). On MAGNITUDE the shipped level is the defensible one.
limit: The real spread is 50:1 across six cars, so magnitude alone cannot settle a round. The statistic that can is CONTENT, and on that one both render arms are indistinguishable from painted sheet metal - see car-glass-content-anchor in the same directory.
